11.1e — Create PT: Build Day 4 + List Check

Last build day before the writing/recording days (11.2a). Today: freeze, audit, and the ritual this whole year trained you for — the requirements checklist, done out loud, with witnesses. A PT that passes the audit twice cannot be surprised on submission day.

Audit Day ~30 min

The audit ritual — partner swap, read-aloud verification. One of you points, one of you checks the rubric language:

RequirementEvidence, on screen or in codePass?
List participating in program functionWhere is it added to, removed from, or traversed — IN the behavior path?☐
Procedure with ≥1 parameterName it, show the signature, show the call passing values☐
Algorithm: sequencing + selection + iterationPoint at one line for each of the three☐
The CALLWhere does a call trigger the algorithm from the program's actual behavior?☐
Input → behavior → outputTrace one user input to one visible output☐
Video plan under 60sRehearse with a stopwatch: demo path intact?☐

Partner's signature on your CPT_PLAN.md, and yours on theirs. This is 8.6's review ritual, aimed at College Board instead of your teacher.

Bug Hunt: Audit findings

  1. Your list participates but the video will not SHOW it (the behavior happens internally). What needs upgrading — the program or the demo path?
  2. The parameter exists but callers pass the SAME constant every time. Why would a grader doubt the parameter's purpose — what variation proves it matters?
  3. You found a crash on input "" (empty). Fix or guard? Which one makes a better WR2b answer (defensive check: "handles empty input by ___")?
Freeze + Writing Installments ~20 min

Freeze means freeze. After today: no new features, no refactors, no "small improvements." Every change after this point risks the demo path — and your WR answers must describe the FINAL code, not the aspirational one.

WR installments (draft all five in CPT_PLAN.md — prompts here):

  1. WR1: purpose + problem solved + abstraction managing complexity (you have answered this all year — your palette class, the UnityEvents, the singleton...)
  2. WR2a: the algorithm, explained (your 11.1c paragraph)
  3. WR2b: the development story — describe ONE difficulty you faced and the fix. TODAY's bug-hunt findings ARE this answer: write one down while you still remember the debugging session.
  4. WR2c: the list — what it stores, how the program uses it. One paragraph.
  5. The video script: the demo path as a numbered shot list.

Tinker: Close the build

  1. Tag it: git tag cpt-build-final && git push --tags.
  2. Commit + push: "11.1e: FROZEN + WR drafts".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Pass the six-row audit with a partner's signature
  • Explain every requirement by pointing at your own code
  • Show all five WR drafts in the plan file
  • Resist new features until submission (the freeze discipline)
